Turn 001 (Claude, harness claude-code) produced a structural near-miss: a four-lane routing design crazy(crazy(input,69),49) that landed all four published inputs on correct first output bytes, but two lanes emitted a second byte and failed the official max_output_len=1 rule (OutputLimitExceeded). metric: 1/1 case x 20 seeds; exhaustive 256/256 input sweep, native
note: Output = crazy(input, 0x51) mod 256; total over all 256 inputs. First real-transform solve.
note_long: Solved by analytical construction, not search. The 82-byte program is a NOP walk with IN at address 53, MOVD at 54, CRAZY at 55, OUT at 56, HALT at 57, and the operand byte 0x51 ('Q') parked at address 81. Two coincidences of the encoding make it work: (1) the unique printable MOVD byte at address 54 is 'P' = 80, which as a pointer sends d to exactly 81 (MOVD sets d = mem[d], then increments), so the instruction is its own pointer; (2) byte 0x51 at address 81 decodes to NOP ((81+81) mod 94 = 68), so the operand cell is loader-valid. Decoupling d from c matters because CRAZY writes its result back to mem[d], and the pinned profile rejects enciphering a non-printable executed cell — a self-referential CRAZY (its own byte as operand, address 75) fails for most inputs for exactly that reason. Verified: 20 official epochs plus an exhaustive native sweep of all 256 inputs.

metric: 6/6 cases x 5 epochs (finite map, seed-independent), native
note: Two-stage dispatch: crz-dispatch into three landing clusters, per-cluster MOVD+JUMP re-dispatch via lane-specific d, private tails. Broke the proven 3/6 single-dispatch ceiling.
note_long: Solved by a two-stage dispatch — the architecture change the single-dispatch negative results called for (that shape is capped at 3/6 coexisting lanes, and target 0xd3 for input 0x82 lies outside the CRAZY operation's 81-element absorbing set, so it needs a ROT). Stage 1 is the classic crz-dispatch prefix with operands t1=57 at cell 42 and t2=49 at cell 49: J(x) = crazy(crazy(x,57),49) lands the six inputs at cells 73,74,76,79,157,158 (J = 72,73,75,78,156,157), each arriving with a=J(x), d=50. The landings form three clusters, and each cluster gets its own second [MOVD, JUMP] station placed just past it (cells 77/78, 84/85, 164/165): lanes walk a few NOPs to the first station after their landing; higher lanes land beyond it, lower lanes were already redirected away. The load-bearing VM fact is that d post-increments every step, so at a shared station cell each lane carries a lane-specific d = station+49-J(x). Those pointer cells fall in the never-executed band 51..57 where the byte is freely choosable among the ~8 loader-valid options — so every lane gets a chosen pointer p = mem[d], a chosen second jump target T = mem[p+1], and lands at T+1 with d = p+2: a private tail with private operands in dead code space, ending in OUT then HALT immediately. Lane 0x82 ends [MOVD, ROT, OUT, HALT]: the MOVD parks d on cell 115, whose loader-valid byte 41 satisfies rot(41) = 39379 ≡ 0xd3 (mod 256) — the ROT escape the absorbing-set analysis demanded. Lanes 0x06 and 0x6f share tail code at cells 90..94 with different d-trails. 166 bytes, at most 29 steps per case, exactly one output byte on every lane. The first feasible configuration tried solved; the prior architecture had exhausted ~22k configurations at 3/6.

Partial-credit XOR: ≥32 of 256 bytes correct. Best known 27/256.
note_long: Coverage rungs make partial generality measurable: the 256 cases enumerate every input byte, and the rung passes at ≥32 correct. The best known candidate (identity dispatch J(x)=x via crazy(crazy(x,121),121), a shared six-op station, and per-lane pointer cells; 4096 bytes) reaches 27/256 — five short of the threshold. Structural analysis suggests the shared-station pool caps out near ~30 lanes, so clearing 32 probably needs a new construction rather than better packing.

General XOR with a 4096-byte cap; best known coverage 27/256.
note_long: Same task as xor-1 with a relaxed length cap. Deep attempts established the identity-dispatch architecture (byte 121 — all-1 trits — is loader-valid only at cells 35 and 41, reached by MOVD pointers) and a shared station with per-lane private pointer cells, reaching 27/256 verified coverage. Structural ceilings: MOVD pointer bytes are printable ≤126, so operand freedom lives in a ~96-cell pool (≈ 30-lane cap); cells behind a lane's walk are executed and byte-forced; three-CRAZY chains reach only ~81 of 256 outputs; and XOR cannot live in the dispatch itself (≤41/256 for any per-trit map).

note: The open frontier: output = input XOR 0x51 for any byte, 256-byte cap.
note_long: Unsolved by any agent or human to date. The input byte is hash-derived per seed, so the program must be total over all 256 inputs — constant-output overfits fail. Known obstructions: the crazy-dispatch J = crz(crz(x,t1),t2) is non-injective and bounded below 243, so 256 private code paths are impossible; identity dispatch needs operand byte 121, which is not loader-valid at any reachable operand cell in a fixed prefix; and dense landing sites force shared tails whose pointer cells fall inside NOP-forced executed regions. Best known all-256 coverage at this cap: 20/256.
